title: Zaalouk
subtitle: Moroccan cooked aubergine and tomato dip
excerpt: One of the most popular Moroccan salades cuites (cooked salads): aubergine and tomatoes simmered together until very soft and mashed into a rough, fragrant dip with cumin, paprika, and a generous pour of olive oil. Served warm or at room temperature with bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Zaalouk is one of Morocco's most beloved salades cuites — the category of cooked vegetable salads served at room temperature as starters or meze alongside bread and other dishes. The dish is widespread across Morocco and is closely related to similar preparations in Algeria and Tunisia. Aubergine (eggplant) and tomatoes are the core, seasoned with the characteristic Moroccan combination of cumin, sweet paprika, and often a little cayenne or harissa for heat. The aubergines can be roasted whole then peeled (which gives a smokier result) or peeled, cubed, and cooked directly in the pan. The final texture should be rough and scoopable: neither a smooth purée nor chunky like a stew. A generous final pour of olive oil is essential; it enriches the dip and gives it its characteristic sheen.

recipeTools.notes: A wide frying pan or saucepan.

content.text: Salt the aubergine before cooking to draw out moisture: this step speeds cooking and concentrates the flavour. Cook the mixture until it is very soft and most of the liquid has evaporated; the final dip should not be wet. Mash roughly with a fork rather than blending; the texture is part of the appeal. Add the raw garlic and lemon juice only at the end to preserve their brightness.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes; salted and rinsed after 20 minutes
3 finely chopped for cooking, 1 raw and grated for finishing

content.text: Heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil in a large, wide pan over medium heat. Add the drained aubergine and the 3 chopped garlic cloves. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 minutes until the aubergine is very soft and beginning to colour.

Add the tinned tomatoes, cumin, paprika, and cayenne. Cook over medium heat, stirring and mashing frequently, for 20 to 25 minutes until the tomatoes have reduced completely and the mixture is thick and jammy. Remove from the heat.

Mash roughly with a fork to a coarse, chunky paste. Stir in the raw grated garlic, lemon juice, coriander, and parsley. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Transfer to a serving plate. Drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Serve warm or at room temperature with flatbread.
